screens.marker: GROUND\s+POINTS[\s\S]*W o r k i n g
ERROR!\s+(?:LEFT|RIGHT)\s+Bank Station DOES NOT MATCH a Ground Point
DEPTH is Greater than the DIAMETER

source: Critical flow in a circular section: Q = A sqrt(g A / T) at depth y, with A = D^2/8 (t - sin t), T = D sin(t/2), t = 2 acos(1 - 2y/D), Chow (1959), Open-Channel Hydraulics. The drawn discharge stays under the critical discharge at 0.9 D, so the critical depth falls inside the pipe. A judgement, not an observation of QUICK-2: Critical Depth printed the same Max Discharge at slopes .005 and .001 (cd-circ-000001, cd-circ-000002, Q-009), so a bound from the typed slope is not used for it.

Manning's equation for a pipe flowing full, Q = (1.486/n) A R^(2/3) S^(1/2) with A = pi D^2/4 and R = D/4 (D in ft), Chow (1959), Open-Channel Hydraulics. A judgement that bounds the drawn discharge, not an observation of QUICK-2.

Chow (1959), Open-Channel Hydraulics, Table 5-6, as reproduced in USACE HEC-RAS Hydraulic Reference Manual 6.6, Table 3-1 Manning's n Values (natural streams, flood plains, lined and excavated channels): least minimum 0.011 (concrete trowel finish, glazed brick, smooth steel), greatest maximum 0.500 (vegetal lining). https://www.hec.usace.army.mil/confluence/rasdocs/ras1dtechref/6.6/basic-data-requirements/geometric-data/energy-loss-coefficients

Chow (1959), as reproduced in USACE HEC-RAS Hydraulic Reference Manual 6.5, Table 6-1 Manning's n for Closed Conduits Flowing Partly Full: least minimum 0.008 (Lucite), greatest maximum 0.030 (corrugated metal storm drain, cemented rubble masonry). https://www.hec.usace.army.mil/confluence/rasdocs/ras1dtechref/6.5/modeling-culverts/culvert-data-and-coefficients/manning-s-roughness-coefficient

AISI (1980), as reproduced in USACE HEC-RAS Hydraulic Reference Manual 6.5, Table 6-2 Manning's n for Corrugated Metal Pipe: greatest value 0.033 (6 x 2 in. corrugations, 60 in. diameter, unpaved). https://www.hec.usace.army.mil/confluence/rasdocs/ras1dtechref/6.5/modeling-culverts/culvert-data-and-coefficients/manning-s-roughness-coefficient

AISI (1980), as reproduced in USACE HEC-RAS Hydraulic Reference Manual 6.5, Table 6-2 Manning's n for Corrugated Metal Pipe: diameters listed from 8 in. (0.667 ft) to 180 in. (15 ft). QUICK-2 asks for Diameter (in), so the bounds are in inches (cd-circ-000001, solver Requirement 4.4). https://www.hec.usace.army.mil/confluence/rasdocs/ras1dtechref/6.5/modeling-culverts/culvert-data-and-coefficients/manning-s-roughness-coefficient
